visualAssessment.finding: The page now distinguishes resource context, title selection, related assignment facts, the current operation and the queue. The single assignment surface groups owner/next/durations; the queue has a consistent reading rhythm. No clipped or overlapping required text remained in the inspected current states. This is a restrained candidate within the original palette, not a newly approved visual identity.
corrections: Initial admin-like treatment revised through grouping, role prominence and consistent checkboxes.
Broken narrow Russian title replaced by a full-width navigation row.
Narrow settings error moved out of the scrolling body next to the footer actions; failure also restores keyboard focus.
Modal screenshots restricted to the real viewport rather than synthesizing below-viewport backdrop pixels.
limits: Enlarged text deliberately increases vertical page length; the data queue still has its own scroll owner.
Narrow settings require scrolling inside the body; top and bottom states were inspected.
One author and one pilot do not establish independent taste, user recognition or future generation quality.

stateFindings.finding: Selected title is distinct; holder, next, duration and action remain one related group. Empty states have no artificial tall well.
Text remains readable and complete. Enlargement changes line and tab wrapping; it is accessibility stress, not an alternate default density.
Long title is whole; field labels, units, footer actions and both scroll positions remain legible.
Reference aliases and IDs are present in their proper context. Separate operations have distinct destinations; no second settings entry appears.
State/recovery copy is local to the task. Disabled actions remain distinguishable from available supporting operations.
Current data is retained and the recovery message is visible near the affected operation. The settings footer error was checked after repair.
